title: Merlin the Enchanter
subtitle: Arthur's magician
subject: mythologie
description: Merlin, Arthur's counselor, prophet and magician: a figure born of a demon and a baptism, architect of Camelot, prisoner of his own love.

hero.hook: Son of a demon, baptized in the cradle: Merlin serves good with powers born of evil.

blocks.text: **Merlin** is the most famous magician of the Western Middle Ages. Bard, prophet, counselor to King **Arthur**, he stands on the border between the old Celtic world and Christian knighthood.

His nature is a paradox. One part of him comes from the demons, the other from heaven. His story is not a magic show: it is the struggle of a hybrid being who chooses to serve good, until love takes him out of the world.

sections.title: A hybrid origin: demon and baptism

blocks.text: In the poet **Robert de Boron** (12th century), the demons want to create an antichrist. An [[incubus demon]], a spirit that lies with a sleeping woman, seduces a devout young Christian. The plan fails: the mother confesses and has the child baptized.

blocks.caption: Merlin, the medieval magician between forest and court

blocks.text: The name “Merlin” comes from the Welsh **Myrddin**. Geoffrey of Monmouth changed the “d” into an “l” to avoid a pun too close to the Latin *merda*.

His [[baptism]] wipes out the curse but leaves the powers: knowledge of the past, a demonic inheritance, and the gift of [[prophecy in medieval culture]]. Merlin can change shape. Behind him stands **Myrddin Wyllt**, a Welsh bard of the 6th century who went mad after a battle and fled into the forest of [[Celyddon]].

Merlin is not a conjurer. He is the guarantor of the kingdom. He helps King [[Utherpendragon]] take on the face of the duke of Cornwall so he can reach the duchess **Igraine**. From that night **Arthur** is born.

blocks.caption: Merlin guides Arthur toward the throne and Camelot

blocks.text: He raises the child in secret, stages the sword in the anvil, then leads Arthur to the Lady of the Lake to obtain [[Excalibur]], whose scabbard guards against mortal wounds. At **Camelot**, he designs the **Round Table** and sets in place the [[Siege Perilous]], the empty seat kept for the purest knight. He sees the dangers coming. He also knows that destiny always gets its way in the end.

sections.title: The fall of the enchanter: love and oblivion

blocks.text: Merlin knows how he will end. He falls in love all the same with **Viviane**, the Lady of the Lake, near the spring of Barenton. He teaches her his most secret spells, even though he knows she will be his undoing.

blocks.caption: Viviane shuts Merlin away: the end of the age of magicians

blocks.text: Depending on the version, Viviane traps him in a hawthorn bush, a tower of glass or a hollow in **Brocéliande**. Immortal, Merlin is not dead: he sleeps outside the world.
When the knights set out for the Grail, Merlin's magic has no place left. His withdrawal marks the passage from the age of myths to the age of faith.

sections.title: A literary legacy and the figure of the archmage

blocks.text: Merlin fixed the image of the old wise man: beard, staff, riddles. **Gandalf** in Tolkien and **Dumbledore** in Rowling both descend from him. He is the helper who knows, but who cannot act in the hero's place.

A bridge between the wild forest and the court, he keeps a [[druidic]] imprint even as he advises kings. Even today he whispers that empires are fragile, and that wisdom does not always protect you from yourself.
**Merlin**, born of a demon and saved by baptism, builds the destiny of **Arthur** and then disappears, prisoner of **Viviane**: the lasting model of the Western enchanter.
